title: Molecular Resonance Chamber
description: The user operates a molecular resonance chamber where the SpecularSilkPouf represents a reactive polymer gel sample and the BoomBox serves as a sonic frequency emitter used to trigger molecular phase transitions. Users must calibrate frequency, amplitude, and exposure duration across multiple steps to achieve the target crystalline phase without destabilizing the sample.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a Molecular Resonance Chamber experiment. Load both GLB assets using GLTFLoader. Place the SpecularSilkPouf at the center of the scene on a circular platform, representing a polymer gel sample. Place the BoomBox on a rail to the left, representing a sonic frequency emitter aimed at the sample. Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 3, 6) with OrbitControls. Add ambient light (intensity 0.4), a directional light from above-right, and a point light near the BoomBox that changes color based on the active frequency. Create an HTML overlay control panel with these interactive steps: (1) A frequency slider (20-2000 Hz) that rotates the BoomBox model slightly toward the sample and changes the point light hue accordingly. (2) An amplitude slider (0.1-10.0) that scales the SpecularSilkPouf pulsation animation. (3) A 'Begin Exposure' button that starts a 5-second countdown timer, during which the sample visually vibrates using sinusoidal position offsets. (4) A phase indicator display showing the current molecular phase: Amorphous, Semi-Crystalline, or Crystalline, computed from frequency and amplitude values. The target is Crystalline phase, achieved only when frequency is between 800-1200 Hz AND amplitude is between 4.0-6.0. (5) A 'Stabilize' button that locks current parameters and changes the sample material emissive color to green if crystalline, red if destabilized (amplitude > 8), or yellow otherwise. (6) A 'Record Result' button that logs the trial to a visible results table below the viewport. Validate all parameters before each step proceeds. Add particle effects (small spheres) emitting from the BoomBox toward the sample during exposure using a simple particle system. The sample should glow with increasing intensity as it approaches the crystalline phase. Display a success banner when a crystalline result is recorded.
